verdict.rationale: Both refactors look behavior-preserving. Each replaces the u8 state with an enum, routes every error to Done in one place, and splits the scanning into small helpers backed by a large differential check. A also adds seven regression tests to the repo that pin the edge cases (empty values, `a==b`, quote errors, nested brackets, separator errors, invalid escapes), so the next person editing the tokenizer is protected. B adds no tests. A's design of pure scan functions returning a Step keeps all state and position changes in next(), while B spreads state mutation across methods.
a_issues: Report leans optimistic on speed ("possibly a few percent faster") from noisy benchmarks, though it does flag a 2–3% cross-crate gap and asks for a real-dump check.
The Step struct and the closure-based `find` helper add a little indirection compared with plain loops.
b_issues: No tests added to the repo; the edge-case coverage lives only in an out-of-repo scratch harness.
State changes are scattered across methods (scan_key_or_word sets Value, scan_value resets to Start before scanning), which makes the control flow harder to follow than a single bookkeeping point.
Scatters #[inline] and #[inline(always)] hints as a performance workaround, with only noisy evidence that they help.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors appear to keep the original tokens, errors and positions, and both back that with large differential runs. B also adds seven regression tests that pin the edge-case errors and positions a future edit could break, and it passes on the original code. A adds no tests, so its equivalence check lives only in a scratch harness outside the repo. B's pure scanner functions that return a `Step` are a bit cleaner than A's mutating methods with a boolean flag argument, and B's benchmark makes a better case that it is not slower.
a_issues: Adds no tests; the edge-case equivalence it checked lives only in an out-of-repo scratch harness
`scan_plain(bytes, start, stop_at_equals: bool)` uses a flag argument, which is less clear than passing the stop condition
State changes are split between the scan methods (`scan_value` resets the state before scanning) and `next()`, so the bookkeeping is not fully in one place
Uses `#[inline]`/`#[inline(always)]` hints chosen from noisy 1-3% measurements; benchmark is inconclusive by its own account
On error, `pos` is no longer moved to the end of the line, which also changes the derived `Debug` output (harmless, but the report does not mention it)
b_issues: The generic `find` helper with closures is a small extra layer of indirection
Has not been benchmarked on a real dump either, though it says so in the report
